```{r}
path <- file.path('results','fit_indices',params$run_id)
indices <- c('rmsea','cfi','tli','srmr')
files <- file.path(path,paste0('summary_',indices,'.csv'))
if (!all(file.exists(files))) stop('Missing compacted ML production. Run scripts/compact_production.R INPUT_DIRECTORY OUTPUT_DIRECTORY; see Reproduce.')
source('R/judge_production.R')
summary <- do.call(rbind,lapply(files,read.csv,stringsAsFactors=FALSE))
cells <- read.csv(file.path(path,'cells.csv'),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
j <- judge_production(summary,cells)
targets <- read.csv(file.path(path,'targets.csv'))
failure_counts <- read.csv(file.path(path,'failure_counts.csv'))
affected <- read.csv(file.path(path,'harness_affected_draws.csv'))
show_table <- function(x, digits=4) {
  names(x) <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub('_',' ',names(x)))
  cat(as.character(knitr::kable(x,digits=digits,format='pipe')),sep='\n'); cat('\n\n')
}
```

## Default register

```{r, results='asis'}
register <- data.frame(index=toupper(j$decisions$index),estimator='ML',
  point='Misspecification-robust',interval='None',status='Decided by approved rules',
  evidence=paste0('768 cells × 1,000 attempts; ',params$run_id))
register <- rbind(register,data.frame(index=toupper(indices),estimator='FIML (MAR 15%, 30%)',
  point='Misspecification-robust',interval='None',status='Pending production',evidence='Not evaluated here'))
show_table(register)
```

The approved rules retain all four ML point defaults and select no interval.
Neither candidate point correction is eligible for any index. Lavaan-robust
CFI and RMSEA have no losses, but their 44 and 29 wins respectively fall short
of the required net improvement in at least 10% of 768 cells (at least 77).
All available interval methods fail the coverage rule; the square-root Wald
method additionally fails availability. These are decisions from the frozen
ML run, with no retuning and no library default changes. FIML remains pending.

## Question and decision rules

Which point corrections and 90% intervals should ordinary users receive for
RMSEA, CFI, TLI and SRMR? The [approved criteria](criteria/fit_indices.md) were
recorded before production. A point candidate wins a cell at RMSE at most
0.9 times the default's, and loses when the default's RMSE is at most 0.9 times
its own. Eligibility requires losses no greater than wins in **every model
family**, and at least 77 net wins across the 768 cells for that index.

An interval needs at least 95% availability in **every cell**, coverage outside
87.5–92.5% in at most 5% of cells (at most 38 of 768), and coverage at least 80%
in every cell. Among eligible methods, the smallest median width decides.
Coverage uses available converged draws; availability uses all 1,000 attempts.
Undefined coverage is reported separately and cannot establish eligibility.
The retained cell width is the mean available-draw width; the comparison table
shows the median of those cell means. No method reaches the width tie-break.

A family is one model, estimator setting and index. Family bias and RMSE below
combine its 64 cells using the available-draw counts; wins and losses still
use each cell's own RMSE and population target. No cross-family average
replaces a family eligibility check. Population RMSEA, CFI and TLI are
**outcomes of the delta grid**, not preset fit-index levels; exact values are
retained in `targets.csv` and the cell tables.

## ML production and failures

The production has 768 cells, each with 1,000 attempted draws: twelve tier-1
models, four standardized misspecification sizes, four sample sizes and four
generators. All population targets are available. The run used seed base
2026101001, runner commit `5a7330bc` and library build `dd6325ad`.

The harness defect affects **312 draws in 29 cells**: 299 `cfa_second12`,
11 `sem_worland11` and two `cfa_bifactor15` draws. It occurs **after a fit
fails the library convergence verdict**. The old code pasted the ten-field
`lab$verdict` list into a reason vector, then assigned that vector to a
24-row arm table. The runner caught “replacement has 10 rows, data has 24”
and retained all 24 arms as unavailable. These were not converged fits lost
to an interval calculation. Reproduction of second-order CFA, delta 0,
N=200, discretized generator, replicate 154, seed 2071474585 confirms a failed
stationarity verdict and the exact error. The fixed harness reads the scalar
`lab$verdict$status` and returns 24 unavailable rows with `not_converged: failed`.
The branch causing the defect is entered only for nonconverged fits.

No ML cell was rerun. The frozen summaries retain these failures and all
attempted denominators. The complete draw/cell inventories and the reproduction
are `harness_affected_draws.csv`, `harness_affected_cells.csv` and
`harness_diagnostic.csv`. The repair applies to future runs, including FIML.

```{r, results='asis'}
conv <- unique(summary[c('cell','convergence')])
show_table(data.frame(attempted_draws=sum(cells$N*0+1000),
  converged_draws=round(sum(conv$convergence*1000)),
  minimum_cell_convergence=min(conv$convergence),
  harness_defect_draws=nrow(affected),affected_cells=length(unique(affected$cell))))
f <- aggregate(count~reason_class,failure_counts,sum)
names(f)[2] <- 'unavailable_arm_index_rows'
show_table(f)
```

Failure counts count arm/index rows, rather than distinct draws: a failed draw
contributes 24 such rows. Structural absence remains in the denominators.
Lavaan supplies no robust SRMR point correction and noncentral intervals only
for RMSEA; the unavailable arms fail eligibility rather than disappearing from
the comparison. The square-root Wald arm is undefined when the corrected
discrepancy is not positive. There is no SRMR interval arm in the registered grid.

## Per-index results

The following tables are calculated from the compacted frozen summaries.
Each index includes every model family, every candidate loss and the complete
interval cell grid in expandable tables. CSV links retain unrounded precision.

```{r, results='asis'}
for (index in indices) {
  cat('\n### ',toupper(index),'\n\n',sep='')
  cat('The rules retain the misspecification-robust point and no interval.\n\n')
  show_table(j$candidates[j$candidates$index==index,c('arm','wins','losses','losing_families','eligible')],digits=3)
  cat('#### Point results by family\n\n')
  show_table(j$family[j$family$index==index,c('model','arm','availability','bias','rmse','wins','losses','ties','unavailable')])
  losses <- j$losses[j$losses$index==index,c('cell','arm','target','rmse','default_rmse','availability')]
  loss_path <- file.path(path,paste0('point_losses_',index,'.csv'))
  cat('Every loss against the default (',nrow(losses),' candidate–cell losses) is retained in [the loss CSV](',loss_path,').\n\n',sep='')
  cat('<details><summary>Every point loss</summary>\n\n')
  show_table(losses)
  cat('</details>\n\n')
  if (index=='srmr') {
    cat('Lavaan-robust SRMR is structurally unavailable in all 768 cells. No SRMR interval candidate was registered.\n\n')
    next
  }
  cat('#### Interval eligibility\n\n')
  show_table(j$intervals[j$intervals$index==index,c('arm','min_availability','availability_failures','flagged','undefined_coverage','below_floor','min_coverage','median_cell_width','eligible')])
  interval_path <- file.path(path,paste0('interval_cells_',index,'.csv'))
  cat('Coverage, width, availability, flags and targets for every cell are in [the interval CSV](',interval_path,'). A flag means coverage outside 87.5–92.5%; the floor is 80%.\n\n',sep='')
  cat('<details><summary>Every interval cell (conditional coverage and mean width)</summary>\n\n')
  show_table(j$interval[j$interval$index==index,c('cell','arm','target','available','availability','coverage','width','flag','below_floor')])
  cat('</details>\n\n')
}
```

## Cost and uncertainty

```{r, results='asis'}
timing <- read.csv(file.path(path,'timing_summary.csv'))
timing <- merge(timing,cells[c('id','model')],by.x='cell',by.y='id')
model_cost <- do.call(rbind,lapply(split(timing,timing$model),function(x)
  data.frame(model=x$model[1],mean_seconds_per_draw=mean(x$mean),
    median_cell_median_seconds=median(x$q50),largest_cell_p95_seconds=max(x$q95),
    sampling_cpu_hours=sum(x$mean*x$attempted)/3600)))
show_table(model_cost,digits=3)
```

Cost measures sampling, including all arms, separately from target preparation.
Per-cell timing quantiles are in `timing_summary.csv`; setup costs and target
diagnostics are retained separately. The sum of sampling seconds is CPU time,
not simbox wall time. At 90% coverage, 1,000 available draws give a Monte Carlo
standard error of about 0.95 percentage points; fewer available draws increase
that error. The flag band and floor are applied as registered, with no
multiple-comparison adjustment or post-results widening. RMSE comparisons also
have sampling error; eligibility here is the registered empirical decision,
not a significance test.

## Caveats

ML is the only production evaluated here. This result does not settle FIML,
DWLS, ordinal data or other missingness laws. Conditional coverage can look good
when availability is poor; both are reported and both are gating. Retained
floating-point population targets and frozen boundary conventions are used
without rounding targets for judgment. No failed fit is removed from attempted
denominators. The retained draw used to diagnose the harness is development
data for future fixes; it is not fresh confirmation evidence.

## Targets and conventions

The generating h1 population gains the catalog's omitted block. Every coefficient
in the block has the same standardized size: residual covariance divided by the
disturbance standard deviations, or loading/regression multiplied by the ratio
of predictor and outcome total standard deviations. The core supplies implied
moments; inadmissible generating populations fail before sampling. A cell may
specify the signed size directly or root-find the continuous population RMSEA
within absolute standardized size .4.

The RMSEA target is $\sqrt{G F_0/\mathrm{df}}$. Complete-data targets fit h1 and the independence baseline to population moments
with the lab fitter, starting from the default fit's estimates and refining with
`control = list(nlopt = list(ftol_rel = 1e-14, xtol_rel = 1e-12,
max_eval = 10000))`. The library convergence verdict remains required. Default
and refined diagnostics (Newton distance, budget, iterations and verdict) are
retained. The installed library reports zero iterations for these fits; the
record preserves that field rather than inferring evaluation counts. Failed targets remain listed with unavailable target-based summaries;
sampling costs and arm availability remain measurable. RMSEA uses the number of groups; TLI uses nominal
degrees of freedom. Each MAR-FIML target uses one fixed 200,000-row draw with the
same generator and masking law as its cell. The saturated/user/baseline likelihood
contrasts are library components. This finite integration approximation has Monte
Carlo error; it is recorded with its seed and method, and is not an exact MAR
integral. Complete-data targets are retained beside estimator-specific targets.

The MAR law masks half of the variables independently conditional on one fully
observed cause. Its logistic slope is one after standardizing the cause, and the
intercept calibrates the expected rate in each draw and group. The configuration
can instead name the cause and targets. Fifteen percent means fifteen percent of
each target column, rather than fifteen percent of all entries.

Normal single-group data use the core model generator; grouped normal data use
Cholesky draws. Vale–Maurelli data use centered cubic Fleishman transforms and
inverted intermediate normal correlations. Independent-generator data apply a
covariance factor to independent Fleishman variables. The latter's configured
skewness and excess kurtosis describe the independent sources, not each observed
variable. Integer discretized scores use equal-probability thresholds with
Pearson-code correlation calibration. Their variances and means are the exact
score moments, so their own population targets are recomputed; a requested RMSEA
sizes the continuous parent, not the scored population. Every configured generator
must reproduce its own population covariance within 1% relative Frobenius error
in a separate million-row check. Infeasible calibrations fail without matrix repair.

Naive and lavaan-robust points use the lab compatibility composer (MLM for complete
ML, MLR for FIML). The ordinary `fit_measures()` supplies the adopted corrected
points. The lab supplies naive/scaled noncentral RMSEA intervals and both 90% Wald
variants. Noncentral CFI/TLI intervals and lavaan-robust SRMR are unavailable
components, retained with reasons. The square-root Wald variant can be unavailable
at zero corrected discrepancy. RMSEA lower bounds are clipped at zero and zero is
covered when that bound is zero. Conditional coverage, attempted-draw coverage,
availability and convergence are all retained per cell; no fit is discarded.

## Retained pricing and memory evidence

The earlier 48-cell/240-draw pricing pilot establishes harness plumbing only;
it does not enter the ML decisions above. TASK-149's bounded long30 diagnostic
preserved all 72 result rows while reducing worker peak RSS from 642 to 397 MiB.
Its frozen memory/provenance CSVs remain under `results/task149/`; FIML memory
remains unmeasured.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, with the lane library read-only:

```sh
Rscript experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/scripts/compact_production.R \
  /path/to/original/2026-10-09-ml-b \
  experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/results/fit_indices/2026-10-09-ml-b
R_LIBS=~/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-c OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  nice -n 10 Rscript experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/scripts/diagnose_arm_failure.R
R_LIBS=~/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-c quarto render experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/report.qmd
```

Compaction reads the frozen originals and writes bounded summaries plus derived
decision tables. `input_checksums.csv` identifies every original CSV; metadata
preserves command, seed, source, library and criteria provenance. Large
`summary.csv`, `failures.csv`, `timing.csv` and per-draw checkpoints remain ignored.
The originals are retained in the main checkout's result directory; raw rows stay
on simbox at `~/magmaan-runs/magmaan-main-5a7330bc/experiments/decisions/09-fit-indices/results/fit_indices/2026-10-09-ml-b/raw/`.
The report reads only this study's compacted results and never runs estimation.

The production command is retained in `metadata.csv`. Future production needs a
fresh run ID after this harness change; strict source/library/config/seed/criteria
fingerprints prevent resuming old checkpoints with changed code. No ML rerun is
needed for these decisions. FIML remains under the same approved criteria.
